mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within two months signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a decline in consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in the previous two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the quarters where GDPC1 declined by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 2% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE was below 5% and PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates a broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST decreased by more than 10% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was above 2% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.3% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as increased consumer spending supports corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of the months where RSAFS increased by more than 1%.
